fullPassage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been fashioned therein. And while artists may enhance, exaggerate, or take artistic license with that representation to satisfy their client, to make an artistic statement, or to challenge hegemonic norms, the manner in which the body is fashioned in an artwork provides clues to the expression of aesthetic ideals and norms for that period in history. These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments depicted, how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included. As Anne Hollander, a historian of art and dress, expressed in her book Seeing Through Clothes, “clothes make, not the [wo]man, but the image of the [wo]man,” such that art and clothing are “connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking.”

② practical — 원문은 aesthetic(미적인). 예술적 표현이 드러내는 것은 실용적 이상이 아니라 미적 이상이므로 practical은 부적절 ←정답

④ connected — 연결된, connected links 원문 일치

questions.passage: When artists represent the human form in works of art, the narratives of culture become embedded in the manner in which the body has been fashioned therein. And while artists may enhance, exaggerate, or take artistic license with that representation to satisfy their client, to make an artistic statement, or to challenge hegemonic norms, the manner in which the body is fashioned in an artwork provides clues to the expression of aesthetic ideals and norms for that period in history. These clues might include the posture, gaze, and stylization of the body of the sitter, the extent to which the figures are dressed or undressed, the types and colors of textiles and embellishments depicted, how the hair is fixed, and what accessories or props are included. As Anne Hollander, a historian of art and dress, expressed in her book Seeing Through Clothes, “clothes make, not the [wo]man, but the image of the [wo]man,” such that art and clothing are “connected links in a creative tradition of imagemaking.”
